title: One shape, five independent bugs

findingsItems.label: the liveness check reads res.ok, not status — a killed session still answers 200, so resume reports success in 0.7s having resumed nothing
queue: true omitted → a mid-turn prompt is silently dropped
the resume cursor stays frozen → every reply after a resume vanishes
an account-pinned inbound route → never fires, filtered out silently

title: Credentials are per-member, not per-room
bullets: A shared room holding one key shares it with everyone who has the code.
Our position: each member attaches their own tools over rendezvous — nothing inherited.
Revocation is an unpair, not a key rotation — there was never a shared secret to rotate.

title: Built on our own open-source runtime
bullets: Unmodified. Installed from npm. No fork, no vendored copy.
The room layer is every line that's new — the judged artifact.
8 upstream findings, shipped as a maintainer write-up (docs/UPSTREAM.md).

title: What was simulated, what was observed
bullets: Runs 1–2: simulated inbound, no phone, no agentpush workspace. Run 3: real Telegram + web, live.
Paused e2b boxes expire in 20–60 min — and tonight it happened live: box i7jos61ixgkcfrekmi1vl expired mid-rehearsal, and the room kept advertising its now-dead artifact URL.
Resume-after-kill and the dead artifact link: fixed after rehearsal, re-proof pending. A room-scoped, proxied artifact URL is now being built — ahead of whisper and multimodal.
We share the default workspace's Telegram routing — its existing responder route can fire alongside ours on the same message, risking a double reply.
WhatsApp: not provisioned. No number, no key.
Phase 2 pairing-back: untested — box-to-broker egress, which side mints the token, post-pairing scope.
